title: Rational objects on universally closed stacks over algebraically closed fields
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $\mathcal Z$ be a nonempty algebraic stack over $K$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Suppose $\mathcal Z$ admits a smooth surjective atlas by a quasi-compact scheme, and its diagonal $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal Z\times_K\mathcal Z$ is quasi-compact and separated. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of stack morphisms have the chart conventions of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]; separated for a representable morphism means its relative diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume that for every $K$-scheme $T$ the map $|\mathcal Z\times_K T|\to|T|$ sends closed subsets to closed subsets, with the point spaces and $2$-fibre products of [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets, def-pc-scheme]. Then $\mathcal Z(K)$ has an object: there exists a $K$-morphism $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal Z$. No local finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis on $\mathcal Z/K$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 0DQL (lemma-gerbe-diagonal-quasi-compact), 0DQQ (lemma-sober-qs), 06RC (proposition-open-stratum), 06R9 (lemma-gerbe-bijection-points), 06QI (lemma-gerbe-fppf), and 0DN8 (lemma-gerbe-smooth); together with decent-spaces.tex Tag 047Z (lemma-when-field) and morphisms.tex Tag 01WM (lemma-integral-universally-closed). This is the same-field existence input implicit in Alper Theorem 5.3.1(5), following the argument of Good moduli spaces Theorem 4.16(iv); an independent proof is outlined in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-qc-diagonal-stack-spectral] to $\mathcal Z$: its quasi-compact smooth atlas and quasi-compact diagonal are hypotheses of the item. Its nonempty point space is therefore quasi-compact and Kolmogorov. By [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point] choose a closed point $z$. By [lem-sfb-smooth-presentation-closed-subsets] the closed subset $\{z\}$ has a reduced closed substack $i:\mathcal C\hookrightarrow\mathcal Z$ with $|\mathcal C|=\{z\}$.

The diagonal of $\mathcal C$ is the base change of the diagonal of $\mathcal Z$ along $\mathcal C\times_K\mathcal C\to\mathcal Z\times_K\mathcal Z$: closed substacks are full, so the isomorphism spaces between their objects are unchanged. It is quasi-compact, since any further quasi-compact scheme test is exactly a test of the original diagonal [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. For each $K$-scheme $T$, [lem-sfb-stack-closed-immersion-calculus] makes $i_T$ a closed immersion inducing a closed embedding on point spaces. Thus every closed subset of $|\mathcal C\times_K T|$ is closed in $|\mathcal Z\times_K T|$, and its image in $|T|$ is closed by the assumed universal closedness of $\mathcal Z/K$.

Apply [lem-sfb-reduced-singleton-qc-diagonal-gerbe] to $\mathcal C$: reducedness and the singleton point space came from step 1, and step 2 supplies its quasi-compact diagonal. Obtain a field extension $L/K$ and a gerbe $p:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}L$. By [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism], $p$ is smooth and surjective and remains a homeomorphism on point spaces after every algebraic-stack base change.

Let $T$ be any $K$-scheme and write $Y_T=\operatorname{Spec}L\times_K T$. Base changing the homeomorphism assertion of [lem-sfb-gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism] along $Y_T\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ gives a homeomorphism $|\mathcal C\times_K T|\to|Y_T|$. For a closed subset $D\subseteq|Y_T|$, its inverse image is closed; its image in $|T|$ is closed by step 2 and equals the image of $D$, by surjectivity of that homeomorphism. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is universally closed. It is affine (the inverse images of the only affine opens of the field spectrum are affine), so [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed] says that $L$ is integral over $K$.

For $a\in L$, integrality supplies a monic polynomial over $K$ vanishing at $a$. Since $K$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], this polynomial factors into linear factors over $K$ (successively divide by a root); since $L$ is a field, one of those factors vanishes at $a$. Thus every $a\in L$ belongs to $K$, and the structure inclusion $K\to L$ is an isomorphism. Regard $p$ as a smooth surjective map $\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}K$.

Smoothness of $\mathcal C$ over $K$ means, by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], that there is a smooth surjective scheme atlas $U\to\mathcal C$ whose composite $U\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is smooth. The atlas is nonempty because $|\mathcal C|$ is a singleton. The algebraically closed field $K$ is separably closed: its irreducible polynomials are linear. Hence [lem-pc-rational-points-dense] supplies a $K$-point of $U$. Compose $\operatorname{Spec}K\to U\to\mathcal C\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal Z$. This is the required object of $\mathcal Z(K)$.

split_report.summary: Checked the no-finite-type hypotheses directly against Stacks. Choose a closed point using spectrality, pass to its reduced closed singleton substack, identify that substack as a gerbe over a field, descend universal closedness through the gerbe homeomorphism, and force the field extension to be trivial before selecting a rational point on a smooth atlas. Two new statement-only inputs; all other ingredients reused. Statement unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Generic scheme criterion integral = affine + universally closed, applied to the residue field spectrum; the unit has no such criterion.
Generic compact Kolmogorov topology supplies a closed point without finite type; the unit has no such topological lemma.
Generic existence of a rational point on a nonempty smooth scheme over a separably closed field, applied to the gerbe atlas; the unit has no such point-existence lemma.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q50-f298b89d4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement, and checked them against the Stacks sources. Spectral node: it is exactly 0DQN lemma-spectral-qc-diagonal-qc (stacks-morphisms l.6721). The diagonal relative to Spec k and the absolute one have equivalent quasi-compactness. The empty stack is allowed. Gerbe node: 06RC proposition-open-stratum (l.6533) needs only a reduced stack with quasi-compact inertia, and the inertia is a base change of the diagonal. The planned route is 06RC, then 0DQL (base space quasi-separated, so decent), then 06R9 (base space a singleton), then 0DN8 (smooth, so the base is reduced), then 047Z lemma-when-field (Spec L); the k-structure factors through the gerbe. Tested on Spec L, BG, a non-neutral gerbe and Spec k(t)/k; no Noetherian or finite-type input is needed. There are no duplicates: noetherian-singleton-gerbe, singleton-stack-finite-field-homeomorphism, flat-inertia-algebraic-space-quotient, unramified-diagonal-singleton-field-cover, finite-type-stack-closed-specialization and quasiseparated-space-sober all have different hypotheses or conclusions. Steps: (1) the spectral node and 005E give a closed point, and smooth-presentation-closed-subsets gives the reduced substack C with |C|={z}. (2) Elementary: C is a monomorphism into Z, so Δ_C is a base change of Δ_Z and quasi-compact; closed-immersion-calculus passes universal closedness to C. (3) The new gerbe node gives p: C→Spec L, and gerbe-smooth-universal-homeomorphism (0DN8/06R9) makes p smooth, surjective and a universal homeomorphism. (4) Base change along Spec L×_K T shows Spec L→Spec K is universally closed and affine, so 01WM gives L integral over K. (5) Elementary: L=K because K is algebraically closed. (6) A smooth nonempty atlas over the separably closed K has a K-point by lem-pc-rational-points-dense. proof_deps is the union of the step citations and there is no cycle. Batch-5 flags: all four flagged citations reach def-trf-algebraic-space only as the general definition of algebraic spaces. They are definitions or general stack topology, not results the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality assumptions give, so they are accepted. tool_uses accepted: 01WM, 005E and rational points on smooth schemes are generic. No SGA. The statement is unchanged; the separated-diagonal hypothesis is simply unused. No fixes.

lean.note: Uses the recorded quasi-compact smooth-atlas predicate and algebraic-space scheme tests for the quasi-compact separated diagonal. Universal closedness is tested on the smooth-presentation topologies of the canonical 2-products with every base scheme. The conclusion is the actual fibre over the identity K-scheme, not an object over an extension. The two added landed definition dependencies supply the canonical base structural morphism and the existing algebraic-space quasi-compactness/separatedness predicates.
